question: Can a declared C-peptide appearance rate be propagated to plasma concentration with independently checked kinetics, and what can noiseless synthetic observations identify?

source.equations: p99 two-compartment scheme and process definitions; p100 unnumbered biexponential bolus equation
source.parameters: p103 Table I, printed group-mean K1/K2/K3 and distribution volume; mean parameters are nominal profiles, not an averaged participant trajectory
source.stimulus: p99 constant infusion: 3 then 30 pmol/(kg min), 120 min each
source.rights: public primary article inspected locally; original equation implementation and factual parameter transcription; no author code or article redistribution

cases.name: bolus
cases.evidence: published analytical equation, synthetic normalized dose; not original 50 nmol cohort decay

cases.name: step
cases.evidence: published infusion schedule replay using nominal mean coefficients; no measured cohort curve comparison

cases.name: basal_pulse
cases.evidence: entirely synthetic baseline and added secretion pulse

identifiability.source: p99 post-bolus times, applied to synthetic noise-free observations only
identifiability.fitting: log-parameter least squares on noiseless independently generated bolus concentrations; fixed known dose; no clinical estimation or general secretion deconvolution

excluded_claims: resolution of BC-001 initialization or secretion scale
failure_policy: preserve attempted inputs, sources, settings and errors; reject incomplete solves and altered/nonfinal archives; never overwrite runs
